findings.area: be/src/game.ts:773 (updateProfile keep-own-name skip) x be/src/names.ts:84-92 (double key, any-key collision)
findings.title: Teacher-name uniqueness and the reserved 'Dr. Claire Moreau' are defeated by a two-step chain: register a name that is NOT in the table, then rename to the table spelling
findings.evidence: Live on :5001. 'Marie Dubois' registered by teacher A. Direct 'Мarie Dubois' (U+041C) -> 409 name_taken (round-11 fix works). But teacher B registers 'мarie Dubois' (lower-case Cyrillic em U+043C, which is deliberately not in the table) -> 201, then PUT /api/profile {name:'Мarie Dubois'} -> 200 and B now holds a name that reads exactly like A's. Same chain for the reserved demo name: register 'Dr. Claire мoreau' -> 201, rename 'Dr. Claire Мoreau' -> 200, and its content review is then recorded as 'Dr. Claire Мoreau (teacher #83)'. Cause: a name has two keys (capital-first, lower-first) and sameName() is true when ANY key is shared, which is not transitive ('m' ~ 'М' ~ 'м' but 'm' !~ 'м'); updateProfile skips assertTeacherNameFree entirely whenever the new name is sameName() as the teacher's CURRENT name, so each hop is judged only against the previous name.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r12-A/chain1.mjs  (node chain1.mjs 5001; also against a server with DEMO_MODE=1 for the reserved name)
findings.expected: A rename to a name that collides with another teacher (or the reserved demo name) is 409 name_taken regardless of the teacher's previous spelling; the OpenAPI text on register/PUT /profile promises exactly this.
findings.actual: 200; two teachers (or a teacher and the demo teacher) display visually identical names; only the '(teacher #id)' suffix tells them apart.
findings.fix_hint: be/src/game.ts:773: skip the check only when the key SETS are equal (nameKeys(new) equals nameKeys(old)), or run assertTeacherNameFree always and let it ignore only the teachers that already collided with the caller's current name (grandfathered twins). Equivalent: make the relation transitive by comparing the union/canonical of both keys.

findings.area: be/src/names.ts (HIDDEN strips bidi controls but does not undo their reordering) + http.ts CONTROL_CHARS
findings.title: A bidi override (U+202E ... U+202C) around the REVERSED text renders as 'Dr. Claire Moreau' or '(teacher #7)' yet folds to a different key, so the reserved-name rule and the '(teacher #n)' rule are bypassed
findings.evidence: Live: register teacher with name '\u202E' + reverse('Dr. Claire Moreau') + '\u202C' -> 201 (stored name '\u202Euaeroμ...'; displayed as 'Dr. Claire Moreau'); its review is returned as reviewedBy '‮uaeroM erialC .rD‬ (teacher #40)' which a browser draws as 'Dr. Claire Moreau (teacher #40)'. Student/teacher name '\u202E' + reverse('(teacher #7)') is also 201 while plain 'Bob (teacher #7)' is 400. The web client renders names with no <bdi>/unicode-bidi isolation (grep web/src: none).
findings.repro: scratchpad/r12-A/live2.mjs (port 5003) and live1.mjs lines 1-2 (port 5001); offline: names2.ts prints 'pass rlo' and DIFF for the reversed demo name
findings.expected: Explicit bidi formatting characters (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) either rejected in display names (they have no legitimate use in a person's name) or folded in a way that cannot change reading order.
findings.actual: Accepted; key is the reversed string so no collision and no suffix match.
findings.fix_hint: be/src/game.ts checkDisplayName (and ideally http.ts validate for the 'name' fields): reject /[\u202A-\u202E\u2066-\u2069]/ with a 400 validation_error; web: wrap names in <bdi>.

findings.title: The most obvious Latin-only lookalikes of the reserved name are accepted: capital I for l ('Dr. CIaire Moreau'), 0/o, 1/l, rn/m, IPA letters (ɑ, ɡ, ᴄ)
findings.evidence: Live: 'Dr. CIaire Moreau' registers as a teacher (201) and as student; names2.ts: DIFF for capI_for_l, digit0, digit1, rn_m, latinAlpha, scriptG, smallcapsC, armenianO, cherokee*, clickL. KNOWN_LIMITATIONS lists Armenian/Cherokee and '0/o, 1/l' as residual but not capital-I/lower-l, the classic same-script confusable, nor the Latin IPA block.
findings.expected: At least I/l/1/| and 0/o (and ideally UTS #39 skeleton) folded for the reserved name; or document it.
findings.fix_hint: names.ts: add 'I'->'l' style folding in a third key (or adopt the UTS #39 confusables skeleton for the reserved demo name only); add the case to KNOWN_LIMITATIONS 'Round 10 notes'.

findings.title: Two legitimately different teachers are refused when their names differ only by a Vietnamese tone mark, an emoji/symbol, or a space
findings.evidence: Live 409 name_taken after the first registered: 'Lê Thị Hà' vs 'Lê Thị Hạ' (different Vietnamese given names, tone mark only), 'Dr. 🧬' vs 'Dr. 🧪' (symbols are dropped from the key whenever a letter exists), 'Li Wei' vs 'Liwei', 'Peña' vs 'Pena'. Accent/space/punctuation folding is documented; tone-only Vietnamese names and symbol-only differences are not called out. Everything else in a 250-name corpus (Latin, Polish, Nordic, Turkish, Cyrillic incl. й/ї/ў/ё, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, CJK, Thai) behaved as designed: no unexpected merge, Devanagari/Thai/CJK/kana all distinct, Greek names do not collide with Latin ones (final sigma).
findings.expected: Documented, or the user told which part to change (the 409 text just says 'another teacher already uses this name').
findings.fix_hint: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: say that tone marks (Vietnamese) and symbols/emoji do not distinguish teacher names; optionally keep Vietnamese tone marks significant (do not fold marks on Latin letters that carry U+0323/U+0309/U+0303 together with a circumflex/breve base).

findings.title: The cleaned hint keeps NUL and lone surrogates: the text returned to the learner differs from the stored/reloaded text (NUL truncates it in SQLite, a leading NUL loses the paid hint on reload); the 400 limit counts UTF-16 units
findings.evidence: Stub provider via test harness: hint 'ab\u0000cd' -> response hint 'ab\u0000cd' but GET attempt hintsGiven[0].text === 'ab'; lone surrogate 'ab\ud800cd' -> reload 'ab\ufffdcd'. A text starting with NUL would be stored as '' and then omitted from hintsGiven (falsy) while the 15 XP was charged. 201 emoji (402 UTF-16 units) is refused although it is 201 characters; 200 emoji (400 units) accepted. Non-string (number/object/array/String object/undefined), blank, 401-char, throwing providers all correctly fall back to the standard hint with source 'standard' and consistent hint_log/hintsGiven/penalty.
findings.expected: Control characters stripped/rejected and the stored text identical to the delivered text.
findings.actual: Divergence for NUL and lone surrogates (only reachable with a real provider that emits them).
findings.fix_hint: game.ts:720: reject (return null) when /[\u0000-\u0008\u000B\u000C\u000E-\u001F\u007F\uD800-\uDFFF]/ matches (lone surrogates via text.isWellFormed()), count [...text].length.

findings.title: OpenAPI says PUT /api/profile requires a request body and lists 409 on POST /api/missions/{id}/start; the server accepts an empty body and never answers 409 there
findings.evidence: Regenerated to scratch (openapi.gen.json): identical to be/openapi.json and to GET /api/openapi.json, structurally valid (0 errors: refs resolve, path params match, 31 operations, statuses, patterns compile). But PUT /api/profile with no body or {} -> 200 while requestBody.required is true; POST /api/missions/hem-01/start only returns 201/401/403/404/429 (startMission has no conflict path).
findings.fix_hint: openapi.ts: emit requestBody.required only when the schema has required[]; drop 'POST /api/missions/:id/start': [409, 429] -> [429].

findings.title: A bad DB_PATH (directory, garbage file, unwritable parent, schema newer than the build) ends with a raw Node stack trace, unlike HOST/PORT/AUTH_SECRET which print one clear line
findings.evidence: DB_PATH=<dir> -> 'Error: unable to open database file' + stack; garbage file -> 'file is not a database' + stack; DB_PATH=/System/x/y.db -> EPERM mkdir stack; schema v99 -> 'Database schema v99 is newer than this build (v7).' inside a stack. Exit code non-zero in all cases, no secrets printed.
findings.repro: run each with DB_PATH=... node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning src/server.ts (see task log in scratchpad r12-A)
findings.expected: 'Escape Lab API cannot start: <reason>' and exit 1.
findings.fix_hint: server.ts: wrap createApp(cfg) in the same try/fatal() used for configFromEnv.

findings.title: db:backup: two simultaneous runs to the same file give one 'Backup verified' and 'database is locked' (exit 1) for the loser instead of the 'Refusing to overwrite' (exit 2) path; an empty path argument prints "Cannot back up to : ENOENT ... chmod ''"
findings.evidence: bk6.sh: 6 parallel runs x 6 rounds, always exactly one winner and the winner's file passes db:check; the losers print either 'Refusing to overwrite' (rc 2) or 'Cannot back up to ...: database is locked' (rc 1). All other round-11 cases hold (file as parent, dangling symlink, unwritable dir, existing file, relative path, spaces/quote in path, WAL DB with a concurrent writer: 6/6 copies verified and db:check clean).
findings.expected: Consistent code/message for 'target already exists/being written'.
findings.fix_hint: db-backup.ts: map 'database is locked' / 'already exists' from VACUUM INTO to the exit-2 refusal; reject an empty argv[2].

findings.title: Class name rule says 'at least 2 visible characters' but counts code points: 'A\u200B' (1 visible) is accepted while 'A\u3000' is refused with a details-less 400
findings.evidence: POST /api/classes: 'A\u200B' -> 201 (stored with the zero-width char), '\u200B\u200BAB' -> 201 (ZWSP kept, not trimmed), 'A\u3000' -> 400 'A class name needs at least 2 visible characters.' with no details array (the schema validator path returns details). Emoji/ZWJ/CJK/variation-selector/supplementary-plane names are all accepted, so the stricter \S pattern rejects no legitimate input I could construct.
findings.expected: Same rule and same error shape in both places.
findings.fix_hint: game.ts createClass: count visible characters (strip INVISIBLE) and throw bad(msg, [details]).

notes:
Environment: node v22.23.2, own servers on 5001 (NODE_ENV=test, DEMO_MODE), 5002 (real limits, DEMO), 5003 (real limits, no demo), 5004 (second process on the same DB), 5011-5016 (six processes migrating one v5 DB), 5021 (kill -9 victim); all on throwaway DBs in scratchpad/r12-A, be/data never touched, no repo file edited, npm run openapi not run (generated to scratch). Baseline: npm test 165/165 pass, tsc --noEmit clean.

What I tried and could NOT break: (1) Route x role matrix, 31 operations x anon/student/teacher/other-teacher/forged-signature/expired/ghost-user/role-lie token: every cell matches the contract (401/403/404), 0 5xx; other-class teacher gets 404 on class, roster, student detail and analytics; student B gets 404 on student A's attempt get/answer/hint/result. (2) Answer-leak scan over a full playthrough of all 10 missions (point, choice, decision, order, match, stepper, Master Lab): start, resume, wrong answer, hint, early result, right answer, result, lobby, vault, unlock, lab results, dashboard, profile, leaderboard, badges: no explanation of an unsolved step, no unbought hint, no recheck outside a wrong-answer response, no exit code before the exit, no banned field (key/answer/solution/radius...); order/match items are not presented in key order. content endpoints are 403 for students. (3) Scoring oracle: independent recompute of 166 random completions (random wrong/hint/time mixes incl. the 0-floor cap) = 0 discrepancies for score, ledger sum, penaltyXp, stats, accuracy, max, XP total, result endpoint. (4) State machine: 12 parallel starts -> 1 attempt; 20 parallel wrong answers -> wrongTotal 20 exactly; 15 parallel correct -> 1 success + 14 attempt_finished; 6 parallel hints -> 2 granted, 4 no_more_hints; post-completion answer/hint 409; out-of-order step and unknown step 409 wrong_step; expiry at exactly the limit (accepted) and +1 ms (rejected), AI hint finishing after expiry rolls the penalty back, clock stepping back clamps elapsed; 10 parallel wrong vault codes -> exactly 5 x 422 + 5 x 429, 8 parallel correct -> one grant, badges not duplicated. (5) Rate limits without NODE_ENV=test: answers 120/min, start 60/min, writes 60/min, join 10/10 min, login 8 per ip+email and 60 per IP (documented lockout #9), XFF ignored without TRUST_PROXY; I also tried to launder the per-IP failure budget with concurrent successful logins (release() pops the last hit): net effect is neutral, 59 guesses allowed per 150 attempts, so no bypass. (6) Input fuzz: 4000 random requests (weird JSON values, __proto__, bad content types, bad paths, bad methods, tokens) + 9 raw malformed HTTP requests: 0 5xx, no log noise; 30 MB bodies -> 413 without memory growth; 20000-deep JSON -> 400. (7) kill -9 under a write load then db:check/invariants (counters vs step_results, mission_best vs attempts, xp_events vs best, unique active attempt, blank names): 0 violations, restart recovers WAL. (8) Demo-off: demo tokens minted with the same secret are 401 on a non-demo server, /auth/demo 404, /demo/reset 404, seeded credentials refused, reserved e-mail domain 400, reserved teacher name still 409; demo reset student/teacher 200, normal student 403.

Other observations not filed: slowloris relies on Node defaults (requestTimeout 300 s, no connection cap) - fine behind a proxy; assertTeacherNameFree scans all teacher names under the write lock (about 38 microseconds per teacher, 0.4 s at 10k teachers - teachers are invite-only); leaksAnswer remains verbatim-only (accents, NBSP, zero-width, hyphenation evade it, and point/order/match/stepper steps have no guard) as documented; R11-A-05 (reset can recreate a twin) is documented behaviour and only the comment changed; HOST=0x7f.0.0.1 is accepted as a host name (resolver treats it as 127.0.0.1).
